title: Word List 8 — Test rehearsal
intro: Five parts, fifty points, laid out the way the real one is. Part III asks you to write the word yourself, and Part V asks for whole sentences — those are the two that catch people out.

parts.name: Part I
parts.title: Vocabulary Matching
parts.how: Choose the letter of the best definition for each word.
defs: to be slow in leaving or going away
a wide, open area or surface; a stretch
to go along with; or to play music for a singer
the state of being held against one's will
suitable for one's needs; handy to have nearby
to translate; to explain the meaning of
one that is held prisoner; or unable to escape
a strong feeling of emotion, especially joy
to get back; to find and bring back
clumsily expressed; or lacking in skill
a thing that makes life easier, such as a lift or a dishwasher
a long journey by a group; or the group that makes it

parts.name: Part II
parts.title: Multiple Choice: Meaning in Context
parts.how: Choose the word that best completes each sentence.

items.q: A clap of thunder will usually ______ a flash of lightning.
items.why: To go along with; to be together. The same word means to play music for a singer.

items.q: The prisoners of war spent four years in ______ before they were sent home.
items.why: The state of being held against one's will. A captive is the person; captivity is the condition.

items.q: A balanced diet and half an hour of walking are ______ to almost anyone's health.
items.why: Being of use; helpful; favorable. It describes a thing that does you good.

items.q: The bus stop at the end of our street is ______ for everyone in the house.
items.why: Suitable for one's needs; making life easier. The noun is convenience.

items.q: From the top of the dune we saw nothing but a grey ______ of water.
items.why: A wide, open area or surface. An expedition would be the journey across it, not the water itself.

items.q: Three ships and ninety men set out on an ______ to find the source of the river.
items.why: A long journey by a group to explore. The same word also names the group that goes.

items.q: That ______ remark about her cooking upset everyone who overheard it.
items.why: Clumsily expressed; not suitable for the occasion. It also means lacking in skill.

items.q: A woman from the embassy was hired to ______ the minister's speech for the audience.
items.why: To translate into another language. It also means to explain, or to understand in your own way.

items.q: Her knowledge of the old maps proved ______ once the search began.
items.why: Too valuable to measure. The in- is not a negative here — it means beyond price.

items.q: A few guests always ______ by the door long after everyone else has gone.
items.why: To be slow in leaving or going away.

parts.name: Part III
parts.title: Synonyms, Antonyms & Word Relationships
parts.how: Write the best vocabulary word on each line. Spelling counts.

items.q: A synonym for helpful or favorable:
items.why: Beneficial — being of use; doing somebody good.

items.q: An antonym for worthless:
items.why: Invaluable — too valuable to measure; priceless.

items.q: An antonym for skillful:
items.why: Inept — lacking in skill, or clumsily expressed.

items.q: A synonym for to get back or to recover:
items.why: Retrieve. It also means to find a thing and bring it back.

items.q: A noun meaning a strong feeling of joy:
items.why: Ecstasy — a strong feeling of emotion, especially joy.

items.q: A verb meaning to go along with, or to play music for a singer:
items.why: Accompany. Both jobs are on the list, so know them both.

items.q: A verb meaning to translate, or to explain the meaning of:
items.why: Interpret. Its third meaning is to understand a thing in your own way.

items.q: The adjective that goes with the noun ecstasy:
items.why: Ecstatic — overjoyed. Watch the ending: -tic, not -sy.

items.q: The noun that goes with the adjective convenient:
items.why: Convenience — a thing that makes life easier. The -t turns into -ce.

items.q: The noun that goes with the adjective captive:
items.why: Captivity — the state of being held against your will.

parts.name: Part IV
parts.title: Parts of Speech
parts.how: Write noun, verb, adjective or adverb for the bold word as it is used.

items.q: The patients made a captive audience for the man with the guitar.
items.why: An adjective here — it describes the audience. On its own, captive is a noun meaning a prisoner.

items.q: The pianist offered to accompany the singer.
items.why: A verb. Accompany is only ever a verb, whichever of its two meanings is in play.

items.q: We liked the air-conditioning and the other conveniences of the apartment.
items.why: A noun — the things themselves. Convenient is the adjective; a convenience is the thing.

items.q: The winners were ecstatic when the judges read out the names.
items.why: An adjective — it describes the winners. The noun is ecstasy.

items.q: A few guests lingered by the door after everyone else had gone.
items.why: A verb. The -ed ending is the clue: it is something the guests did.

parts.name: Part V
parts.title: Application & Critical Thinking
parts.how: Answer in complete sentences, using the vocabulary word correctly.

items.q: Explain the difference between a captive and captivity.
items.model: A captive is the person or animal being held prisoner, while captivity is the condition they are held in, so a panda born in captivity has been a captive all its life.

items.q: Name something in your house that is convenient, and say why. Use convenient in your answer.
items.model: The dishwasher is convenient because it cleans a whole evening of plates while we are busy doing something else.

items.q: Use expedition and expanse together in one logical sentence.
items.model: The expedition crossed a frozen expanse of ice for eleven days before anybody saw land again.

items.q: Why would an inept remark be worse than saying nothing at all? Use inept in your answer.
items.model: An inept remark is clumsy and badly suited to the moment, so it can upset people who would have been left alone by silence.

items.q: Give two different ways a person could interpret something. Use interpret in your answer.
items.model: You can interpret a speech by turning it into another language, or you can interpret a friend's silence as anger when it is really shyness.
